classification.difficultyReason: Use equal opposite angles to equate their bisected halves, then transfer an angle using parallel sides and recognise corresponding angles to prove the bisectors parallel; the diagram supplies the half-angle labels but leaves this proof connection unstated.

content.prompt: In the diagram below, $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. The bisector of $\angle A$ meets $BC$ at $X$. The bisector of $\angle C$ meets $AD$ at $Y$. Prove $AX$ is parallel to $CY$.

spec.description: Right-leaning parallelogram with horizontal BC and AD. X lies on BC and Y on AD. Dashed red AX and CY bisect the opposite angles; paired alpha and phi labels and matching angle marks remain visible. Single arrows mark AB parallel to DC; double arrows mark BC parallel to AD. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a parallelogram; angle BAX equals angle XAD, and angle BCY equals angle YCD. Coordinates derive both bisectors from the side directions.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and angle labels are shown; the required parallelism is not marked.

answer.short:
$AX\parallel CY$.

Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so their halves are equal. Using $BC\parallel AD$ gives equal corresponding angles for $AX$ and $CY$.
answer.worked:
Let $\angle BAX=\angle XAD=\alpha$ and $\angle BCY=\angle YCD=\varphi$, since $AX$ and $CY$ are angle bisectors.

Opposite angles of parallelogram $ABCD$ are equal, so
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha&=2\varphi\\\alpha&=\varphi.\end{align*}$$
Since $BC\parallel AD$, $\angle CYD=\angle BCY=\varphi$ (alternate angles).

Therefore $\angle XAD=\angle CYD$. These are corresponding angles on transversal $AD$, so $AX\parallel CY$.
